quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your front tire goes flat while you are riding, what will happen to the steering?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy. If you notice heavy steering, pull off the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you to be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet or vest makes other drivers see you better. Use it during the day and at night.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make things worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slowly release the throttle, lean forward, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When securing a load on your motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible on your motorcycle. Placing them high, like on a sissy bar, raises the center of gravity and throws off the bike's balance. Spread the load evenly on both sides to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane—it is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Weave within your lane to be more obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give entering vehicles plenty of space to merge safely. If you can, change lanes away from the ramp. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread surface. You do not need to check how reflective your tires are.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones, keep your fingers ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when roads are wet or when your motorcycle needs longer to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular and white with black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume about other drivers?

options.text: They can see your motorcycle as easily as other vehicles.
You do not need to worry about being seen.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids when braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up from braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, and allergies can make you drowsy and affect your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: When traveling on a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: An advantage to keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You can more easily follow the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more space to maneuver.

questions.question: What should you do to control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To maintain control through a turn, look through it by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: To lean the motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How can you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent car drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Drivers entering a highway from an entrance ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left portion of your lane so they can share the lane, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give space to vehicles entering the highway from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it difficult to see.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed at night and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when no other traffic is present. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: They may make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
They don't help improve a rider's visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you.
